ambiguities.text: The EIP does not explicitly state the behavior when PUSH0 is used in EOF (EVM Object Format) contexts
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume PUSH0 behavior is identical in EOF and legacy bytecode formats, with same gas cost and stack semantics.

ambiguities.text: The 'base' gas cost classification is mentioned but not formally defined in this EIP
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'base' refers to the Gbase cost category (2 gas) as defined in the Yellow Paper, same as ADDRESS, ORIGIN, etc.

implicit_assumptions.description: Compilers will be updated to emit PUSH0 instead of PUSH1 0x00 for post-fork deployments
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Without compiler updates, contracts would not benefit from gas savings, though they would still function correctly.

implicit_assumptions.description: The 11.5% of PUSH instructions that push zero represents a significant enough portion to justify the new opcode
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If the actual usage is lower, the benefit of adding PUSH0 would be reduced, though no security impact.

implicit_assumptions.description: No existing contracts use 0x5f as data that gets interpreted as code through jumps
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts with JUMPDEST analysis that treats 0x5f as data could have different behavior post-fork if that data becomes reachable as code.

implicit_assumptions.description: The standard stack limit of 1024 items applies to PUSH0 identically to all other push operations
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Inconsistent stack limit enforcement could lead to consensus failures between client implementations.
